_header: ===== cherrypick manual trading desk — EXPERIMENTAL PROTOTYPE, educational use only =====
_note: Copy to ~/.cherrypick/config/desk.json. The desk places REAL, irreversible orders. Every default is the SAFE one: an absent file refuses every order, and so does a file with any invalid value (one bad cap refuses the WHOLE config). The desk is never armed from this example file. It also needs CHERRYPICK_DESK_EXPERIMENTAL=1 in the environment — the config alone is not enough. Completely independent of every module's enable_live_trading: enabling the desk never enables an automated loop, and vice versa.
_enabled_note: Only a literal true arms the desk ("yes", 1 and "true" do not). Both this AND the CHERRYPICK_DESK_EXPERIMENTAL=1 environment variable are required.
_allowed_accounts_note: Last-4 fragments of the accounts authorized for manual orders, e.g. ["1234"]. Full account numbers never appear here (suite-wide masking rule). An empty list refuses everything.
_allowed_underlyings_note: Underlying symbols the desk may trade, e.g. ["SPY"]. Upper-cased on read. An empty list refuses everything, closing orders included.
_require_defined_risk_note: Refuse any order whose loss is unbounded (net short the upside tail) or not computable (a calendar/diagonal). Only a literal false turns it off, and even then the dollar caps below still apply — an uncomputable worst case can never satisfy a finite cap. Only an order whose every leg is 'buy to close' is exempt.
_max_order_risk_dollars_note: Worst case at expiry, in dollars, that one order may risk, from the payoff diagram. Must be a finite number >= 0; there is no 'no cap' value (null, a string, NaN or a negative refuses the whole config).
_max_order_buying_power_dollars_note: The most buying power one order may consume, as the broker's own preflight reports it. A preflight that reports no buying-power change is refused.
_max_spreads_per_order_note: Quantity cap: how many copies of the structure one order may be (the GCD of the leg quantities — a 2/-4/2 butterfly is 2).
_daily_caps_note: Per ET trading date. Every submit attempt counts — placed, failed or uncertain alike — because a submit that raised may still have reached the broker. Refused and merely proposed orders cost nothing.
_ticket_ttl_seconds_note: How long a proposed order stays confirmable. Clamped to 30-300.
_broker_keyring_service_note: Which existing module's keyring service holds the broker OAuth credentials to trade through. The desk stores NO broker secrets of its own. Borrowing the credentials is not borrowing the permissions: the desk never reads that module's trading flags.
